title: A catalyst claim under cross-examination
promptMarkdown: A closed ideal A ⇌ B system has C=0.100 M, [B]₀=0, k_f=0.0300 min⁻¹ and k_r=0.0100 min⁻¹. A proposed catalyst multiplies both by five. (a) Derive [B](t), calculate equilibrium composition and time to 90% of equilibrium B with and without catalyst. (b) Compare [B] at 20 min. (c) Explain why “more B after 20 min” does not prove a changed equilibrium. (d) Design a bidirectional time-course experiment able to detect changed equilibrium, faster relaxation or catalyst deactivation; include a control, late-time checks and at least one failure of the simple model.
hintLadder: Use A=C−B to obtain a linear differential equation.
Ninety percent of the endpoint leaves ten percent of the initial deviation.
Starting from both sides tests an equilibrium interpretation more strongly than a single trajectory.
